create-entry.name: Create-entry action
create-entry.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: an entry step `op: "create"` (entry_type slug, title, data, metadata, status inbox|draft) makes a schema-validated entry, returns entry_id/slug, sends entry_created at depth+1, previews in a dry run, and makes it once per event (key: correlation id + workflow + target + step, kept in metadata.automation_created).

custom-operation.name: Free-form AI operation
custom-operation.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: an operation step `op: "custom"` carries its own prompt (${…} templates) and output_schema (a JSON Schema object); `see` adds the item, its attachments, images, the workspace persona; the answer is checked (one retry) and is the step output; write_back maps it onto the entry (summary, tags, metadata.<key>), asset or resource; budget, approval mode and min_role apply as for built-in operations. Named, reusable workspace operations are a later phase.

branches.name: Conditional steps (if/else)
branches.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: any step takes `when` conditions evaluated against steps.* / previous.* (same operators); false records it as skipped (not failed), later references read None, and the dry run shows the verdicts.

iterate-aggregate.name: Iterate / aggregate over a target set
iterate-aggregate.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-12: a `collect` step ("Gather items") runs an entry/asset/resource query (a target's keys) and returns rows (each as ${entry.*}/${asset.*}/${resource.*}), count, total and text (a plain list for an AI prompt), up to the target cap; a render step's list images take the rows whole (grid, moodboard). Linked items (2026-10-12): `entries` (the entry a field names), `asset` / `resource` (the entries using one), an asset/resource query's `entry` (what an entry holds, in its order) and `role`, and sort by `position` (a collection's own order). Left: fanning one AI step out over the rows.

relative-dates.name: Relative dates and cron schedules
relative-dates.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-12: every date key of a query (created/updated/published_after|before) takes a relative date (-7d, -12h, -2w, +3d, now, today), read when the run starts; an unreadable date fails the query instead of widening it. Cron schedules compute next_run_at in their time zone and fire (services/cron.py).

asset-resource-targets.name: Assets and resources as workflow subjects
asset-resource-targets.acceptance: Delivered (2026-10-08/11): asset_*/resource_* events bind `asset.*` / `resource.*`; targets take entity asset|resource; an operation step on an asset sees its image and writes back through a `write_back` field map. Delivered 2026-10-12: the entries linked to a given asset or resource (`asset` / `resource` query keys). Delivered 2026-10-12: `checksum` (and `exclude`) in an asset query; `asset.checksum` in a run. Derived-asset lineage is part of media-adapters.

workflow-approvals.name: Approval step inside a workflow
workflow-approvals.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: an `approval` step parks the run (snapshot in workflow_approvals), asks members at its role (push, Automation → Approvals, app badge), resumes from the next step with ${steps.<id>.output.decision} (approved | denied | expired | stale — the entry changed after it was asked), expires hourly, and lets integration actions marked requires_approval run in an approved run. One-tap Approve/Deny on the push is a later slice.

waits.name: Durable waits and delays
waits.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-13: a `wait` step — `for` (30m, 12h, 3d, 2w) or `until` a date/datetime with `offset` and `at`, in the workspace's time zone, calendar arithmetic across clock changes — parks the run (workflow_waits, the run's snapshot incl. its inputs); a minutely sweep resumes it with the entry as it is then; the entry in the Trash or the workflow switched off/changed cancels it; a moment already past goes on at once (late); a year at most.

idempotency.name: Per-step idempotency keys
idempotency.acceptance: A webhook/integration step with `idempotency_key` (templated) that already succeeded for that key within the window is skipped and its recorded output reused; two concurrent duplicate events deliver once.

media-adapters.name: Image, file and audio processing adapters
media-adapters.acceptance: Slice 3 delivered 2026-10-12: media ops extract_text (a PDF's text layer; scanned pages and pictures by the vision model, image.read_text), pages (PDF pages as pictures, pypdfium2), find_sensitive and redact (faces, plates, personal text by the vision model, pixelated in a new copy).
